objection.quote: So the hypothesis of Lemma 4.1(b) holds, and some ordering of $P\cup N$ has chain value $g\le\frac{S}{2^m-1}$.
objection.witness: NON-SEQUITUR: chain value was defined using decreasing order, but Lemma 4.1 proves only that some possibly different ordering has the desired residue. Order matters: for {10,9,8,7,5}, decreasing order has residue 5, whereas order 10,8,7,9,5 has residue 1. Indeed P={8,7,5}, N={10,9} satisfy sums 20 and 19 with no subset sum strictly between them, so the lemma's premises hold while the decreasing residue of P∪N is 5. No argument shows decreasing order preserves or lowers the residue.
objection.load_bearing: The subsequent XY strategy explicitly takes B={b_1≥⋯≥b_r} with the decreasing-order chain value supplied by Theorem 4.2. The proof has not established the existence of such a B, so the all-n counterstrategy is unsupported as written.
